Sculpt a Weathered Rock with DynaMesh + ClayBuildup + DamStandard + TrimDynamic

Look at `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.obj`. It contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named StartingBall, is a smooth UV sphere of radius 0.5 BU centred at origin, with ~512 faces (lat-lon 16 x 32 tessellation). The SubTool has no polygroups beyond the default, no UVs, and no polypaint.

Load this OBJ into ZBrush, DynaMesh it to a uniform high resolution, sculpt it into a weathered rock with ClayBuildup (coarse base shape), DamStandard (sharp cracks), and TrimDynamic (flat trim planes), then export the result as `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj` (OBJ format). Rename the SubTool to Rock before export.

The exported `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj` must satisfy:

- Exactly one SubTool, named Rock.
- Face count in the range [30000, 100000] (DynaMesh produces many faces; any reasonable working resolution yields this range).
- The mesh is manifold: every edge is shared by exactly two faces.
- The total discrete curvature (sum over edges of (1 - <n_i, n_j>)) is clearly non-zero, confirming the mesh is not a smooth sphere anymore.
- At least 100 vertices have low local normal variance (< 0.05), confirming the presence of the flat trim regions.

No polygroups, UVs, or polypaint are required.
